text:
Maya (design): quick pulse check — working on the 'Create Resource' flow. two questions: 1) inline field-level errors vs. compact top summary for dense forms? 2) required-field signal: asterisk only, or the word 'Required' under label (esp for a11y)?
Jordan (pm): leaning summary for really dense forms where users batch-create. summary + inline for the first item that errors. keeps scannability.
Sam (eng): fwiw runtime: inline errors are cheaper UX-wise but increase DOM/painting when we render error banners. summary-only helps perf for lists with 50+ rows.
Kai (a11y): asterisk alone isn't reliably read by some ATs. prefer explicit text "Required" that can be linked with aria-describedby. if we do asterisk, we need clear label in the legend and programmatic indicator.
Maya (design): what about tone? current error copy is terse: "Name required". thinking softer: "Please enter a name for this resource." keep short but helpful.
Jordan (pm): agree on helpful copy. also we need to decide for destructive actions — modal with typed confirm vs inline undo? different use-cases.
Sam (eng): typed confirm is frictiony but very strong for destructive ops that are irreversible. undo toast is good for accidental deletes if we can guarantee backup retention.
Kai (a11y): typed confirm can be problematic for screen reader users if not implemented carefully (focus trapping + clear instructions). if we go typed confirm, aria-live announcements should explain the format and expectation.
Maya (design): proposal: for form errors use a compact top summary with count + first error anchor + inline hints on focus. Required markers: show asterisk + visible "Required" on hover/tooltip and include explicit text for screen readers via visually-hidden span.
Jordan (pm): +1 for anchors. Also for destructive: use typed confirm for destructive deletes of customer data (one-off), but default to inline undo for bulk operations where we can restore quickly.
Sam (eng): implementation note: for the visually-hidden span we can reuse our .sr-only class and populate with `aria-label` on the input, or a `aria-describedby` pointing to the helper. Minimal JS.
Kai (a11y): also set `aria-live="polite"` on the summary container so assistive tech gets notified without interrupting. and ensure the error summary isn't focus-stealing — let keyboard users tab into it intentionally.
Maya (design): microcopy suggestions: top summary header -> "We found X problem(s) with this form" vs "Please fix these errors". which feels better?
Jordan (pm): "We found X problem(s) with this form" feels less accusatory. keeps tone neutral.
Sam (eng): agreed. also include inline helper text: "Required — we need this to provision resources." for one-off critical fields.
Maya (design): quick poll: inline-first vs summary-first? react with :one: for inline-first (show inline errors as they appear) or :two: for summary-first (only show summary initially, reveal inline on focus).
RedwoodBot: You have new reactions on this message. :thumbsup:
Kai (a11y): my vote is :two: — summary-first reduces cognitive load for dense forms and lets AT users get the sweep quickly. but must ensure errors are discoverable when navigating by keyboard or screen reader.
Jordan (pm): tally so far: :one: Sam, :two: Maya, Kai, Jordan. looks like summary-first wins but let's do a small usability test.
Maya (design): thanks — I'll mock two variants (summary-first + inline-on-focus, and inline-eager). will post screenshots & a short prototype. tagging @Sam for implementation feasibility and @Kai for a11y review before we ship copy changes.
Sam (eng): can do. will check perf impacts on large lists and reuse existing error components.
Kai (a11y): happy to review. reminder: include keyboard flows in the prototype (skip links to errors, focus order).
Maya (design): cool — expect mocks by EOD tomorrow. :sparkles:
